2025.EP15.3.s:
This report responds to the Board recommendation from report EP9.10 adopted at its meeting of April 25, 2024, where the Board directed staff to provide a letter of support to tenants and event organizers at Exhibition Place for events held between May 1 and September 30, 2024, to be considered as Municipally Significant to apply for a Special Occasion Permit or a temporary extension of premises and/or hours for the sale of alcohol at permanently licensed locations on a trial basis, and that staff report back to the Board with an update on the pilot.

Exhibition Place is Canada’s most extensive entertainment venue, hosting more than 1,761 events and attracting more than 5.5 million visitors annually. This iconic entertainment, music, and events site is pivotal in Toronto’s cultural and economic fabric, generating over $594 million in annual economic impact. The grounds, with their multiple venues for sports teams, entertainment, music, and cultural events, are ideally situated to support the nighttime economy.

The 2024 trial was well received and there were no complaints. Staff recommend the continuation of the program in 2025 and on, thereon on an annual basis.

In 2026, the World Cup will be expanded to 48 countries and 104 matches from the current 36 countries, playing 64 games. There will be six matches held at BMO Field.

The event is the world's most watched sporting occasion, attracting a global viewership of four billion people throughout the competition and over 200 million for each match. Overseen by the International Federation of Football Association (FIFA), the World Cup provides significant economic and cultural benefits to host cities. On June 16, 2022, it was announced that the City of Toronto would serve as an official Host City.

As directed by the City Council in 2022, the FIFA World Cup Toronto 2026 Staff Secretariat was established to support the planning, preparation, and execution of the event.

Toronto, North America’s fourth largest City is home to Exhibition Place. The site currently hosts more than 2,000 events annually generating $595 million in economic impact to the City with approximately 5.5 million visitors per year for exhibitions, conventions, events, entertainment, and other activities. Exhibition Place is evolving into a year-round destination, offering a broad range of events and experiences. 2025.EP20.1.t: Cybersecurity Audit of Exhibition Place - Phase One: Physical Security, User Access Management and Staff Training
2025.EP20.1.s:
The Exhibition Place is an agency of the City of Toronto and managed by the Board of Governors of Exhibition Place. As Canada’s largest exhibition and convention centre, the Exhibition Place is used for conventions, conferences, trade shows, entertainment and sporting events, public celebrations, festivals, and cultural attractions, generating over $594.5 million per year in economic impact.

Technology plays a vital role in all aspects of the Exhibition Place's operations and services. Given the size of the operations, and the services that Exhibition Place provides, the Auditor General included a cybersecurity audit of the Exhibition Place in her 2025 Work Plan.

This audit is conducted in two phases. Phase One of this audit focused on:

• Physical security at selected facilities,

• User access management, and

• Social engineering and staff awareness.

Phase Two, which is in progress, will include an overall assessment of Exhibition Place's networks, systems, and application security and will be reported to the Board in April 2026.

This report includes five administrative recommendations. The confidential findings and recommendations are contained in Confidential Attachment 1 to this report.
